sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *lamentablemente* from B2 Unit 1, and the other stance adverbs: *francamente*, *en rigor*, *precisamente* and *apenas*. A stance adverb steps outside the sentence and shows how you see a fact, or how exact it is. In writing about art and history you use them to say what is a pity, what is exact, and what is barely known.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: Lamentablemente, el terremoto de 1650 dañó muchos edificios de Cusco.
En rigor, la Escuela Cusqueña no era solo de Cusco.
*en rigor*: strictly speaking, the exact truth
Precisamente en la catedral está la Última Cena de Zapata.
De muchos pintores apenas se conoce el nombre.
*apenas*: barely; no commas, right before the verb

items.spanish: Lamentablemente, el terremoto de 1650 dañó muchos edificios de Cusco.
items.english: Unfortunately, the 1650 earthquake damaged many buildings in Cusco.

items.spanish: En rigor, la Escuela Cusqueña no era solo de Cusco: sus obras se vendían por toda la región.
items.english: Strictly speaking, the Cusco School was not only from Cusco: its works were sold throughout the region.

items.spanish: Precisamente en la catedral de Cusco está la Última Cena de Marcos Zapata.
items.english: It is exactly in Cusco cathedral that Marcos Zapata's Last Supper hangs.

items.spanish: De muchos pintores apenas se conoce el nombre.
items.english: Of many painters the name is barely known.

sections.content: A stance adverb takes a comma after it at the start of a sentence: *Lamentablemente, ...*. Use it to give your own view or to make a fact exact, and keep the rest of the sentence factual.
